near_miss.lead: ON fé + garðr (property, homestead) ~ Ved. paśú- + gṛhá- in wealth lists
near_miss.why_not: ON hits are legal prose (fé veghanda; bera ut fe; konongs garð), Vedic are prosperity prayers listing cattle, horses, offspring, houses; no shared syntax or figure, just two common words for wealth and the homestead.

near_miss.lead: genealogical 'X dóttir Y, systir Z' ~ Ved. 'asurāṇāṃ duhitā ... devānām svasā' / Gk θυγάτηρ ... πατρός ... μητρόθεν
near_miss.why_not: Kin terms used to identify people are universal in genealogy (saga, Herodotus, AV); the Vedic line is a mythological epithet of a plant, not a genealogy. Nothing distinctive beyond the inherited kin words themselves.

near_miss.lead: killing father and mother: ON 'drepr faður sin eða moðor' ~ Ved. 'mā vadhīt pitaraṃ ... mā mātaraṃ' ~ Hdt. ἀποκτεῖναι ... πατέρα οὐδὲ μητέρα
near_miss.why_not: The ON phrase is in the context line of an item list of outlaw crimes, with a different verb (drepa, not *gʷʰen-/*wedʰh₁-); father+mother as victim pair is the obvious way to say parricide; the BS-39d96 pivot is about paternity, not killing.

near_miss.lead: ON 'stoð ... veldi með bloma miclum' ~ Lat. stare ... aevi florem
near_miss.why_not: Search: ON 'standa með (miklum/beztum) blóma' is a common internal Norse idiom (Bandamanna saga, Laxdæla, Konungs skuggsjá, homilies), probably from learned Latin influence ('floruit'); Lucretius' stare (fixed times) and florem aevi (prime of life) are not in one construction. Not inherited.
Only a legal formula for returning a loan safe; no partner in the bundle uses a cognate of heill or heim in a homecoming phrase (caelo is a mis-mapping, see error line).

error.evidence: Context: battle, he won three ships from the force of Þórir; ván 'hope' makes no sense.

error.correct_reading: hlýddi, pret. of hlýða 'listen' (third normalized variant of 'hlyddi hlyddi lýddi')
error.evidence: The triple of forms is the edition's variant layer for one word; lýða 'people' is wrong.

error.correct_reading: vist f. 'presence, stay' (bera við vist sína 'testify according to his presence'), from *wes- 'dwell'
error.evidence: Witness clause: testify to what he heard and saw while present; víss 'wise/certain' does not fit 'uist sína' (fem. acc. with possessive).
caelum is not the cognate of ON heill / OE hāl; the mapping appears to rest on a surface likeness.
